sector: Agricultural implements (tractor-operated and tractor-mounted: seeders, laser levellers, rotavators, straw reapers, briquette machines)
headline: FY26 revenue of Rs 4,139.70 m is 4.3x FY25 mainly because the Company took over two promoter-owned businesses on 01-Apr-2025; on the issuer's own proforma base revenue grew 63.1% and PAT 51.7%, but FY26 operating cash flow was 8.6% of PAT, one customer is 25.2% of revenue and the offer is made under the 75%-QIB route.
red_flags: Reported FY26 revenue Rs 4,139.70 m vs Rs 959.26 m FY25; proforma FY25 Rs 2,537.60 m gives +63.1% (pp. 87, 92)
FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m = 8.6% of PAT Rs 313.90 m; cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (p. 88)
Top customer 25.21% and top-10 50.04% of FY26 revenue; distributors 46.16% and dealers 39.92% (pp. 29, 36)
EBITDA margin 13.46% FY26, ROCE 31.10%, interest cover 5.03x, debt/equity 1.89x; 78.06% of borrowings repayable within 12 months (pp. 157, 480)
Offer under Reg 6(2): net worth was Rs 5.32 m in FY24; at least 75% must be allotted to QIBs or the Offer fails (p. 57)
Dehlon expansion lifts capacity from 4,000 to 33,000 units for Rs 716.64 m, against 18,219 units produced across both plants in FY26 (pp. 136, 267)
reference_note: Rs 131.69 = lowest listed-peer P/E in the DRHP (Escorts Kubota 23.35x, p. 156) x FY26 basic EPS Rs 5.64 (p. 154). It is our construct for measuring upside, not a price band. For scale: the Oct-2025 allotment to the promoters in the business transfer was Rs 1,547 per Rs 10 share, which is Rs 33.63 per Rs 5 share after the 22:1 bonus and 1:2 split (our arithmetic from pp. 105, 388).

strengths: FY26 EBITDA Rs 557.38 m, margin 13.46%; proforma FY25 margin 14.51% (p. 157)
ROCE 31.10% and interest cover 5.03x in FY26 (p. 157)
Current tax Rs 130.30 m = 29.3% of PBT, above the statutory rate (p. 87)
Two integrated plants; FY26 utilisation 73.62% at Cheema and 89.68% at Dehlon (p. 267)
Issuer reports about 13% value share in straw reapers and 30% / 15% / 12% of subsidised super-seeder units in MP / Haryana / Punjab, from an issuer-commissioned report (p. 236)
weaknesses: FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m against PAT Rs 313.90 m (p. 88)
Top customer 25.21% of FY26 revenue; no long-term agreements; dealer contracts terminable on 60 days' notice (pp. 29, 36)
Borrowings Rs 1,344.07 m; debt/equity 1.89x; 78.06% repayable within 12 months (pp. 157, 480)
Audit trail not enabled at database level to 31-Dec-2025 (p. 52)
Promoters disqualified in the past as directors of Jaggatjit Agro Pvt Ltd for non-filing (p. 24)
opportunities: Indian farm equipment market projected at 7.7% CAGR FY26-FY30 per the issuer-commissioned CARE report (p. 129)
Organised segment about 60% of the implements market, Rs 264 bn in FY26 to Rs 415 bn in FY30, per the same report (p. 221)
Rs 185 m of the proceeds repays borrowings (p. 124)
threats: Subsidy-linked demand; State payments have been delayed (p. 57)
Promoter-leased land under the Dehlon plant with 15% escalation every three years (p. 129)
Peers are far larger tractor makers; the DRHP names no direct listed peer (p. 156)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -47.4% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative: no multiple can be stated, and the entire price rests on a turn that has not yet begun.
